comparison.first_binding_shift: F1 cabinet-budget dominated (23/25 FP); F2 thermal-budget dominated (25/25 FP). Under the corrected F2 cabinet reference and replay-matched historical denominator, cabinet power is no longer the first-binding constraint for FP in any of the 25 scenarios; B_ratio (thermal) binds first in all 25.
comparison.left_boundary_random_count: 9/25 under F2 and 9/25 under F1; identical set of 9 scenarios (array_i 6,8,11,14,15,17,21,22,24). Left-boundary status is driven by B_ratio>1 at lambda=1 (8 scenarios) or S_ratio>1 (1 scenario) and is unchanged by the F2 correction. B_cab_ratio<1 in all 9 under both references.
comparison.cabinet_constraint_f1_vs_f2: Under F1, B_cab_ratio was first-binding for FP 23/25 times, capping capacity. Under the corrected F2 cabinet reference and replay-matched historical denominator, B_ratio (thermal) is first-binding for FP in all 25 scenarios, allowing higher unlocked capacity (median 15.4% vs 7.3%).

frozen_interpretation.rule: CI entirely above zero = SUPPORTS_FP; CI includes zero = INCONCLUSIVE
frozen_interpretation.conclusion: The corrected local-date F2 cabinet reference (time-weighted P99 with replay-matched historical denominator) produces a result consistent in direction with the frozen F1 legacy reference. Both support FP over Random at r=1.25. The F2 result is stronger in magnitude. Under the corrected F2 cabinet reference, B_ratio (thermal) is the first-binding constraint for FP in all 25 scenarios, whereas under F1 the cabinet constraint was first-binding in 23/25. The 9/25 Random left_boundary scenarios are identical in F1 and F2 and are driven by thermal (B_ratio) or space (S_ratio) infeasibility, not the cabinet reference.
